title: IBM Links Modular Cryogenic Cells to Scale Multi-Chip Architectures for 2029 Starling Quantum Computer - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM linked and cooled its first two modular cryogenic cells below 15 millikelvin at its Poughkeepsie facility, a hardware milestone toward the 2029 fault-tolerant Starling system, with each module offering 12x the wiring space of prior fridges and capacity for at least 2,000 qubits.

insights.claim: IBM (NYSE: IBM) successfully linked and cooled its first modular cryogenic cells to below 15 millikelvin at its Poughkeepsie, New York quantum facility, a key hardware milestone toward the planned fault-tolerant IBM Quantum Starling system scheduled for delivery in 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: This is a concrete, trackable engineering milestone investors can use to gauge whether IBM's Starling timeline remains credible or is slipping, since modular cryogenics is a prerequisite hardware step.
insights.locator: IBM (NYSE: IBM) has announced the successful linking and cooldown

insights.claim: Initial operational tests showed the dual-module cryogenic assembly cools from room temperature to 4 Kelvin (liquid helium range) in under five days before reaching sub-15 millikelvin base temperatures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Cooldown speed matters for operational uptime and iteration speed of a modular multi-chip quantum system, since faster cooldown supports more frequent hardware swaps or upgrades without extended downtime.

insights.claim: Each rectangular modular cryogenic cell provides 2.75 cubic meters of internal vacuum volume and 0.53 square meters of wiring surface area, up to 12 times more wiring space than IBM Quantum System One's cylindrical 'chandelier' fridges, and is engineered to house and cool at least 2,000 physical qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Wiring density has been a hard physical constraint limiting superconducting qubit scaling; a 12x wiring-space increase per module is a specific, quantifiable unlock relevant to judging IBM's scaling claims relative to competitors using single-chip cryostats.

insights.claim: IBM's proprietary L-couplers, meter-scale cryogenic quantum cables first demonstrated in 2024, enable direct chip-to-chip quantum state transfer and entangling gates between separate QPUs housed in adjacent modular cells.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: L-couplers are the specific interconnect technology underpinning IBM's multi-chip scaling bet; their prior demonstration since 2024 reduces technical risk for the roadmap milestones that depend on them.

insights.claim: IBM's public roadmap calls for installing Quantum Nighthawk processors into the modular cells later in 2026 for system-level testing, linking multiple processors via L-couplers into a unified system with at least 1,000 programmable qubits by 2027, and reaching the fault-tolerant Starling system by 2029.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Gives investors three concrete, dated checkpoints (2026 Nighthawk install, 2027 1,000-plus qubit link-up, 2029 Starling) to monitor IBM's execution against its own public quantum roadmap.
insights.locator: Later this year, IBM will install IBM Quantum Nighthawk processors
